clue.text: Unconventional May Queen going to welcome mobile home

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in a guest, so the shortened name wraps around the other letters
the Queen abbreviation departs, so it is taken out of the guitarist's first name

parts.note: Brian May is the guitarist of the rock band Queen, so May gives his first name BRIAN
R (Regina) is the standard abbreviation for a queen

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so the letters of home are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A free-spirited May Queen is off to greet a caravan arriving at the fête.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May Queen' looks like a festival figure, but May is the guitarist Brian May of the band Queen; 'going' removes the Queen letter, and 'mobile' signals the shuffled home that 'welcome' takes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an artistic, free-living person is described as leading a Bohemian life, ignoring social conventions.

clue.text: Film writer getting to grips with work this person's seen before

indicators.note: gripping something holds it inside, so the pen letters enclose the others

parts.note: a Bic is a well-known brand of ballpoint pen

indicators.note: seen before means placed in front, so the setter's letter precedes the work letters

parts.note: this person is the setter, so I; the 's is read as is
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A screenwriter tackling a project they have already watched.
explanation.definitionFit: A biographical film telling a real person's life story is called by this blended word.

clue.text: Greeting that reveals sign of nerves?

definitions.text: Greeting that reveals sign of nerves?

parts.words: Greeting that reveals sign of nerves?
parts.note: the usual clasp of palms on meeting, read whimsically as a palm that trembles with nerves

explanation.surface: A greeting that betrays anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: The customary greeting by clasping palms, read literally as a tremor, which is a sign of nervousness.

clue.text: Unclear about facing small cocktail on Wednesday

indicators.note: facing means set opposite, so the turned word stands directly before the small word
about means turned round, so the unclear word is read backwards

parts.note: dim means unclear, as dim light
wee is Scottish for small
the tail of cock is its last letter, K

explanation.surface: A fuzzy-headed drinker faces a little cocktail on a Wednesday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' looks like a drink but is the tail of cock. 'about' turns DIM into MID.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of the working week falls on Wednesday, so the hyphenated word means happening then.

clue.text: Outsiders from CAMRA coming up with free bitter

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top, so the two letters are reversed
the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: CAMRA is the Campaign for Real Ale, the British beer lobby
to rid is to free, as in rid of pests

explanation.surface: Real-ale enthusiasts turn up offering bitter beer for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' plays on the beer CAMRA champions; 'coming up' turns CA into AC.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a harsh, pungent smell or taste is bitter and sharp.

clue.text: Disregard majority of rumour and poison being cultivated

indicators.note: ignoring most of the word rumour, four of its six letters are dropped and only two survive

parts.note: bane is an old word for a poison, as in wolfsbane

explanation.surface: Pay no heed to most gossip and toxins spread around a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disregard majority of' drops four of rumour's six letters, its first four, keeping the last two.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a cultivated person is refined and polished in manner, which is what urbane describes.

clue.text: 'Begorra!' in bowdlerised content is colourful

indicators.note: the content of a phrase is what it holds, so the letters sit within these words

explanation.surface: An Irish exclamation inside a censored text is a lively touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Begorra' is a mild Irish oath, a stock example of language a censor might tame.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the word means many-hued, like the arc of colours after rain.

clue.text: Cancel omnibus without anyone initially on board?

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: an annual is a yearly book collecting stories, as an omnibus collects them

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of anyone

explanation.surface: Call off the bus service since no passenger got aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omnibus' looks like a bus, hence the 'on board' surface, but it is a collected volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to declare a contract or marriage void is to cancel it officially.

clue.text: Back Frenchman over delay — one end or other of reactor inside it's blowing up regularly

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the reversed name goes round the rest
back means going in reverse, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: inside places the reactor letter within the delay word

parts.note: lag is a delay, as in time lag

indicators.note: either end of reactor gives the same letter, so its first is taken

explanation.surface: A Frenchman returns, delayed, as a reactor is constantly exploding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing up' sounds like explosions but means enlarging photographs. 'Back' reverses the name to ENER; 'inside' turns the delay into LARG.
explanation.definitionFit: A darkroom device that projects a negative to make bigger prints, which is a photographer's sense of blowing up.

clue.text: One wet acre could be the result of melt

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else, so wet acre is rearranged

explanation.surface: A sodden field might come from snow thawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges wet acre into CEWATER, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen water that has thawed becomes chilled liquid, the product of a melting block.

clue.text: Remind coalition about covering all angles

indicators.note: about here means scattered around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jog the memory of a governing coalition on some matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something, such as a microphone or aerial, that works in every direction around it, covering every angle.

clue.text: Fashionable sad case drinking cuppa as an alternative

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing

indicators.note: something drinking a cuppa takes it inside, so the tea goes within the shell
the case of a word is its outer shell, so only the first and last letters of sad are kept

parts.note: a cuppa is a British colloquial cup of tea

explanation.surface: A trendy but pitiful person sipping tea in place of something stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sad case' is the empty shell of sad, its two outer letters, not a pitiful person.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: doing one thing in place of another, as an alternative, is doing it in its place.

clue.text: Fit of anger with worker at last having shaken off cold

indicators.note: shaking something off gets rid of it, so the cold letter is removed

parts.note: a shoemaker works at a last, the foot-shaped block, so this worker is a cobbler
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper when a labourer has finally recovered from a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' looks like 'finally', but a last is the cobbler's block; 'having shaken off' drops C from COBBLER. To 'throw a wobbly' is British slang for a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: a sudden tantrum or fit of temper is called a wobbler or wobbly.

clue.text: Take this to become invisible?

parts.note: the idiom to take a ... means to withdraw from prominence, and read literally it is a seat at the rear where you are out of view

explanation.surface: A question about how to make yourself disappear.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: taking the rear position means stepping out of the limelight, so you become in effect unseen.

clue.text: Typifies 'Professional' after half of them succeeded

indicators.note: after places the Professional name following the half word
half of a four-letter word keeps two letters; here the second pair of them

parts.note: Bodie was one of the two agents in the British TV series The Professionals
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A professional succeeded after half of them, as is typical.
explanation.walkthrough: The Professionals was a 1970s British TV action series whose heroes were Bodie and Doyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to give concrete form to an idea or quality is to typify or personify it.

clue.text: Tackle missing hours finding energy to make start

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the hours letter is removed

parts.note: a winch is hoisting tackle, gear for lifting
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Lifting gear without timekeeping needs some power to get it going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' looks like 'begin', but here it means a flinch or jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the sense of a sudden involuntary jump or flinch, as when you start at a loud noise.

clue.text: No joke being on edge

parts.note: no in the sense of not a, as in no expert
a tease is a joke or bit of leg-pulling

explanation.surface: It is no laughing matter to be nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone ill at ease is nervous and tense, the opposite of relaxed.

clue.text: Defying being dismissed in brief flamboyant innings?

indicators.note: in puts the dismissal word inside the spree word

parts.note: a fling is a short spell of wild self-indulgence, a cricket innings in a figurative sense
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A batsman's showy little stint ending in dismissal, defying convention.
explanation.walkthrough: An innings is a batsman's turn in cricket, used here for a brief spell of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: openly disregarding a rule or law is flouting it, which is defiance.

clue.text: It's due to keep one from being on time for breakfast?

definitions.text: It's due to keep one from being on time for breakfast?

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the lien letters contain the one

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt that is due is paid
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Something that makes a person late down for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a lazy morning in bed, while its first words also hide the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying in bed late in the morning is an obvious way to miss the breakfast table.

clue.text: Upcoming combination of articles in French and English tackles surprisingly true fence-sitting

indicators.note: to tackle is to grapple with, so the reversed letters hold the others
in a down clue upcoming means read upwards, so the combined articles are reversed

parts.words: combination of articles in French and English
parts.note: the French article la and the English article an share their a when combined

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected order, so the letters of true are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on French and English articles lands surprisingly on the fence.
explanation.walkthrough: The French la and the English an overlap on their shared A. 'Upcoming' reverses them; 'surprisingly' shuffles true, and 'tackles' holds that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone taking neither side in a dispute is impartial, sitting on the fence.

clue.text: This would suit a dirty chat with unexpectedly bad line ringing

definitions.text: This would suit a dirty chat

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the line word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: line in the sense of ancestry or descent, as in being of noble birth

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests an unusual order, so the letters of bad are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smutty phone conversation spoiled by a surprisingly poor connection.
explanation.walkthrough: A chat is a small songbird such as the stonechat, so a grubby one needs a wash. 'unexpectedly' turns bad into DBA, which BIRTH rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden basin of water where small birds bathe is just the thing for a grubby songbird.

clue.text: Left adrift, Bligh — or Christian, at root one of the flock?

indicators.note: set adrift means cast off, so the left letter is removed from Bligh
the root of a word is taken as its base, its last letter

explanation.surface: Captain Bligh cast adrift, or the mutineer Fletcher Christian at heart a sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: Bligh was set adrift by Fletcher Christian in the Bounty mutiny. The question mark flags that this sheep is wild, not in a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a wild mountain sheep of North America with great curled horns, so a member of a flock.

clue.text: Blue a corny colour?

indicators.note: to blue is an old form of blow, to squander or scatter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is blue a clichéd shade?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like the colour but is the anagram signal; the question mark flags 'colour' as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to shade in a drawing with a waxy coloured stick, which children do to colour pictures.

clue.text: Less than reliable peacekeepers go off

parts.note: UN is the United Nations, whose troops serve as peacekeepers
an alarm that goes off sounds

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping forces that rot or explode are not to be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an argument or structure that is not sound cannot be relied upon.

clue.text: South American welcome for rice dish

parts.note: US means American, as in US troops
hi is a welcoming greeting

explanation.surface: A greeting from South America for a Japanese dish.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish or vegetables.

clue.text: More buoyant boat

definitions.meaning: comparative of light, having less weight and floating more easily
a flat-bottomed barge used to carry goods to and from ships

explanation.surface: A vessel that floats better than another.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the comparative of light, and a barge for unloading cargo ships in harbour.

clue.text: Catch fifty in congregation, conceivably

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
at means in, as at home
CH is short for church, a congregation of worshippers

explanation.surface: Fifty fish caught among a church congregation, one might imagine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceivably' flags the loose equation of congregation with church.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the fastening bar on a gate or door is a catch.

clue.text: Your inner racist turned out revolting

indicators.note: turned out suggests something overturned and reshaped, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Your hidden bigot exposed proves disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like 'disgusting' but means rising in revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: people in revolt against authority are rebellious, the sense of rising up in insurrection.

clue.text: Morosely swapping medium for small — that's awful

indicators.note: swapping one thing for another replaces it, so the medium letter gives way to the small one

parts.note: to act grimly is to act morosely, in a gloomy forbidding way
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Gloomily trading a medium shirt for a small one is dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something gruesome or horrible to look at is awful in the sense of inspiring dread.

clue.text: Come across Chelsea — no other — boss in news

indicators.note: no means without, so the other word is removed from Chelsea

parts.note: else means other, as in someone else

indicators.note: in places the boss inside the news letters

parts.note: N stands for new, so news is taken as two of them
a CEO, chief executive officer, is the boss of a company

explanation.surface: A football supporter crosses paths with a Chelsea manager making headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no other' removes ELSE from Chelsea, leaving CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to happen upon something by luck is to meet or find it by accident.
